content.text:
Confirmed: this commit replaced manual UTC-formatted date printing with the Biweekly library using local `Date`/`Calendar` objects but never told Biweekly which timezone to use when serializing — exactly the issue the fix addresses by setting `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 93de21ca4af4279d8ac132e05a7692a7b75730f5

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (80dcd036) changes all four files from calling `Biweekly.write(ical).go(...)` to explicitly constructing an `ICalWriter` and calling `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())` before writing. I ran `git log -p` on each of the four touched files, filtering for `Biweekly.write` and commit headers, to find when that call pattern was first introduced.

**(2) The introducing change:** All four occurrences of the bare `Biweekly.write(ical).go(...)` pattern trace back to the exact same commit, `93de21ca4af4279d8ac132e05a7692a7b75730f5` ("Thu Sep 4 09:04:06 2014"), which migrated the iCal export logic from hand-rolled, UTC-formatted `PrintWriter` output to the Biweekly library. I confirmed via `git show` on `CalendarExport.java` that the old code explicitly formatted dates/times using `SimpleDateFormat` with `TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC")`, but the new Biweekly-based code builds `VEvent`s from local `Calendar`/`Date` objects without ever telling the Biweekly serializer which timezone those values are in. Since `Biweekly.write(...).go()` has no way to know the implicit timezone, it was emitting ambiguous/incorrect time values in the generated `.ics` output — exactly the defect the 2015 fix corrects by setting a default timezone on the `ICalWriter`.

**(3) Evidence:** 
- `git log -p` on `EventEmail.java`, `EventsExportEventsToICal.java`, `CalendarServlet.java`, and `CalendarExport.java` each show the `Biweekly.write(ical).go(...)` call first appearing in commit `93de21ca`.
- The commit stat for `93de21ca` shows it adding the `biweekly-0.3.3.jar` dependency and rewriting all four files simultaneously — a single, coherent migration commit.
- The diff of `93de21ca` for `CalendarExport.java` shows the removal of explicit UTC timezone handling (`SimpleDateFormat` with `TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC")`) in favor of the Biweekly API, with no equivalent timezone configuration added for the new library — the gap later closed by the bug-fix commit.
